newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwaiti MPs' criticism over shooting angers state.
newsitem.headline: Kuwaiti MPs' criticism over shooting angers state.

text.p: Kuwait's government on Tuesday rebuffed accusations made in parliament that it was guilty of doing too little to investigate an attempted assassination of an opposition legislature.

"I will not accept to be accused of protecting a criminal or a thief," acting premier Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah told reporters after a heated debate in parliament over Friday's attempt against liberal MP Abdullah al-Naibari.
Naibari, 61, was shot as he drove to Kuwait City from his beach house. He was hit in the jaw and shoulder. His wife suffered a superficial bullet wound.
MPs have criticised the state for its handling of the investigation and fear the case could be dealt with as a common rather than political crime.
Kuwait has said it had arrested three Kuwaiti nationals and two Iranians in connection with the attack.
"I wonder what is the relation between the suspects and the government," MP Sami al-Munayes told parliament, charging that the suspects were given privileges at the country's expense.

"Those (suspects) have served the thieves of public funds, whom we shall defeat," MP Meshari al-Oseimi said in reference to high profile cases involving alleged illegal profits by some former officials.
Sheikh Sabah, also foreign minister, asked parliament: "Do you want a clash between parliament and the government?"
When asked if the state plans to dissolve the parliament which was elected last October, Sheikh Sabah told reporters:

"God willing we will not be forced to do so. Why do you (media) conclude that the government implies something and you do not hear the accusations by some MPs against the government (suggesting) that it is covering up for criminals."

Many MPs and diplomats say the Naibari attempt was most probably politically motivated but Sheikh Sabah told reporters: "I see that the incident as personal and I do not consider it political unless the judiciary proves that."

Naibari's longtime political partner, prominent former liberal MP Ahmad al-Khateeb, said on Monday night: "The case is not in safe hands and we have the right to worry. I am not stupid I know what is going on in this country. There is a hidden government that is ruling the country."
